ξαινω.def: ξαίνω I. to comb or card wool, so as to make it fit for spinning, Od., etc. 2. of cloth, to full or dress it, Ar. II. metaph. to dress, thrash, beat, ῥάβδοις ἔξαινον τὰ σώματα Plut.:—Pass., ξανθέν mangled, Anth.;—c. acc. cogn., ξαίνειν κατὰ τοῦ νώτου πολλὰς (sc. πληγάς) Dem.

ξανθιζω.def: Ξανθίζω, (ξανθός) to make yellow or brown, by roasting or frying, Ar.

ξανθιησ.def: Ξανθίης, ου, ὁ, Xanthias, name of a slave in Comedy, Ar.;—no doubt he had yellow hair; cf. πυρρίας.

ξανθοκαρηνοσ.def: ξᾰνθο-κάρηνος, ον, (κάρηνον) with yellow head, Anth.

ξανθοκομησ.def: ξανθο-κόμης, ου, ὁ, (κόμη) (= ξανθόθριξ, Pind., Theocr.)

ξανθοσ.def: ξανθός, ή, όν I. yellow, of various shades; of golden hair, Hom.; so, ξανθαὶ ἵπποι bay or chestnut mares, Il. II. Ξάνθος paroxyt., as prop. n. 1. a stream of the Troad, so called by gods, by men Scamander, id. 2. a horse of Achilles, bayard, the other being Βαλίος, dapple, id.

ξανθοτησ.def: Ξανθότης, ητος, ἡ, yellowness, esp. of hair, Strab.

ξανθοτριχεω.def: ξανθοτρῐχέω, (ξανθόθριξ) to have yellow hair, Strab.

ξανθοφυησ.def: ξανθο-φυής, ές (φυή) yellow by nature, ἕλικες Anth.

ξανθοχιτων.def: ξανθο-χίτων, ωνος, ὁ, ἡ, with yellow coat, Anth.

ξανθοχρουσ.def: ξανθό-χρους, ουν, (χρόα) with yellow skin, Mosch.

ξεινηιον.def: ξεινήιον, ου, τό, (ξεῖνος) (ionic for ξενεῖον which is not used) a host's gift, given to a departing guest, Hom.; δῶρα ξεινήια Od.

ξεναγετησ.gloss: one who takes charge of guests
ξεναγετησ.def: ξεν-ᾱγέτης, ου, ὁ, one who takes charge of guests, Pind.

ξεναγεω.def: ξενᾱγέω, I. to be a ξεναγός, Xen., Dem. II. to guide strangers, shew them the sights, Luc.: Pass., impers., ἄριστά σοι ξενάγηται your work as a guide has been done excellently, Plat.

ξεναγοσ.def: ξεν-ᾱγός, οῦ, ὁ, (ἡγέομαι) I. a commander of auxiliary or mercenary troops (ξένοι), Thuc., Xen., etc. (The form is doric; but like many military terms, it was adopted in attic) II. a stranger's guide, Plut.

ξεναπατησ.def: ξεν-ᾰπάτης, ου, ὁ, (ἀπατάω) one who cheats strangers, or who cheats his host, Eur.

ξενη.gloss: a female guest: a foreign woman
ξενη.def: ξένη, ἡ, (fem. of ξένος) 1. a female guest: a foreign woman, Aesch., etc. 2. (sub. γῆ), a foreign country, Soph., Xen.

ξενηλασια.gloss: expulsion of foreigners, an alien act
ξενηλασια.def: ξενηλᾰσία, ἡ, at Sparta, expulsion of foreigners, an alien act, Thuc., Plat., etc. (from ξενηλᾰτέω)

ξενια.gloss: the rights of a guest, hospitality, friendly entertainment
ξενια.def: ξενία, ἡ, (ξένος) 1. the rights of a guest, hospitality, friendly entertainment or reception, Lat. hospitium, Od., Hdt., etc. 2. a friendly relation between two foreigners, or between an individual and a foreign state (cf. πρόξενος), ξεινίην τινὶ συντίθεσθαι, Lat. hospitium facere cum aliquo, Hdt.; κατὰ τὴν ξ. because of their friendly relations, Thuc.; πρὸς ξενίας τᾶς σᾶς by thy friendship with us, Soph. 3. the state or disabilities of an alien, ξενίας φεύγειν (sc. γραφήν) to be indicted as an alien, Ar.

ξενιζω.def: ξενίζω, (ξένος) I. to receive or entertain strangers, to receive as a guest, Lat. hospitio excipere, Hom., Hdt., etc.; ξ. τινὰ πολλοῖς ἀγαθοῖς to present with hospitable gifts, Xen.:—metaph., ὃν Ἄρης οὐκ ἐξένισεν, i. e. who fell not in battle, Soph.:—Pass. to be entertained as a guest, Hdt., attic II. to astonish by some strange sight, Polyb.:—Pass. to be astonished, id. III. intr. to be a stranger, speak with a foreign accent, Luc.: to be strange or unusual, id.

ξενικοσ.def: ξενικός, ή, όν I. of or for a stranger, of foreign kind, opp. to ἀστικός, Eur.; ξενικά the taxes paid by aliens at Athens, Dem.;— τὸ ξ. the class of aliens, Arist.; τὸ ξ. (sc. δικαστήριον) the court in which aliens sued or were sued, id. 2. of soldiers, hired for service, mercenary, Hdt., Xen. τὸ ξενικόν οἱ ξένοι, a body of mercenaries, Ar., Thuc., etc. 3. = ξένιος, hospitable, friendly, Aeschin.:— ἡ ξενική friendly relation, as between host and guest, Arist. II. foreign, alien, Hdt.; ξ. ὀνόματα foreign names, Plat.; of style, foreign, I. e. abounding in unusual words, Arist.

ξενιοσ.gloss: belonging to a friend and guest, hospitable
ξενιοσ.def: ξένιος, η, ον I. belonging to a friend and guest, hospitable, Ζεὺς ξένιος as protector of the rights of hospitality, Il., Aesch.:— τράπεζα ξ. the guests' table, Od.; ξένιός τινι bound to him by ties of hospitality, Hdt. 2. ξείνια, attic ξένια, ων, τά, friendly gifts, meat and drink, given to the guest by his host, Hom.; ξένια παρέσχε δαῖτα as a friendly gift, Aesch.; βοῦν ξένια ἔπεμψεν Xen.; ἐπὶ ξένια καλεῖν to invite any one to eat with you, Hdt., etc.; metaph., θάνατος ξένιά σοι γενήσεται Eur. II. foreign, Pind., attic

ξενισισ.def: ξένῐσις, ιος, ἡ, (ξενίζω) the entertainment of guests, Thuc.

ξενιτεια.def: ξενῑτεία, ἡ, a living abroad, Luc. (from ξενῑτεύω)

ξενιτευω.def: ξενῑτεύω, (ξένος) I. to live abroad, Luc. II. Dep. ξενιτεύομαι, to be in foreign service, Isocr.

ξενοδαικτησ.def: ξενο-δαΐκτης, ου, ὁ, one who murders guests, Eur.

ξενοδαιτησ.def: ξενο-δαίτης, ου, (δαίς) one that devours guests or strangers, of the Cyclops, Eur.

ξενοδοκεω.def: ξενοδοκέω, ionic ξεινο-, to entertain guests or strangers, Hdt., Eur., etc.:—in late Gr. ξενοδοχέω, NTest. (from ξενοδόκος)

ξενοδοκοσ.gloss: one who receives strangers, a host
ξενοδοκοσ.def: ξενοδόκος (δέχομαι) one who receives strangers, a host, Od.

ξενοδοχια.def: ξενοδοχία, ἡ, (from ξενοδόκος) entertainment of a stranger, Xen.

ξενοδωτησ.def: ξενο-δώτης, ου, ὁ, a host, epith. of Bacchus, Anth.

ξενοεισ.def: ξενόεις, εσσα, εν (ξένος) full of strangers, Eur.

ξενοκτονεω.def: ξενοκτονέω, I. to slay guests or strangers, Hdt., Eur. II. to slay one's host, Eur. (from ξενοκτόνος)

ξενοκτονοσ.def: ξενο-κτόνος, ον, (κτείνω) slaying guests or strangers, Eur., Aeschin.

ξενολογεω.def: ξενολογέω, to enlist strangers, levy mercenaries, Dem., etc. (from ξενολόγος)

ξενοπαθεω.gloss: to have a strange feeling, feel strange
ξενοπαθεω.def: ξενο-πᾰθέω, (πάθος) to have a strange feeling, feel strange or shy, Plut.

ξενοσ.def: ξένος, ὁ, I. a guest-friend, I. e. any citizen of a foreign state, with whom one has a treaty of hospitality for self and heirs, confirmed by mutual presents (ξένια) and an appeal to Ζεὺς ξένιος, Hom. 2. of one of the parties bound by ties of hospitality, i. e. either the guest, or = ξεινοδόκος, the host, id., Hdt., etc. 3. any one entitled to hospitality, a stranger, refugee, Od. 4. any stranger or foreigner, Hes., attic:—the term was politely used of any one whose name was unknown, and the address ὦ ξένε came to mean little more than friend, Soph. II. a foreign soldier, hireling, mercenary, Thuc., Xen.
ξένος I. foreign, Soph., Eur., etc. II. c. gen. rei, strange to a thing, ignorant of it, Soph.:—adv., ξένως ἔχω τῆς λέξεως I am a stranger to the language, Plat. III. alien, strange, unusual, Aesch.

ξενοστασισ.def: ξενό-στᾰσις, ιος, ἡ, a lodging for guests or strangers, Soph.

ξενοτροφεω.gloss: to entertain strangers, to maintain mercenary troops
ξενοτροφεω.def: ξενοτροφέω, (τρέφω) to entertain strangers, to maintain mercenary troops, Thuc., Dem.

ξενοφονεω.def: ξενοφονέω, to murder strangers, Eur. (from ξενοφόνος)

ξενοω.gloss: to make one's friend and guest
ξενοω.def: ξενόω (ξένος) I. to make one's friend and guest, Aesch. II. mostly in Pass., with fut. mid. ξενώσομαι: perf. ἐξένωμαι: aor1 ἐξενώθην: 1. to enter into a treaty of hospitality with one, Lat. hospitio jungi, c. dat., Hdt., Xen.; absol., Xen. 2. to take up his abode with one as a guest, to be entertained, Trag. 3. to be in foreign parts, to be abroad, Soph., Eur.: to go into banishment, Eur.

ξενων.def: ξενών, ῶνος, ὁ, (ξένος) a guest-chamber, Eur.

ξενωσισ.def: ξένωσις, ιος, ἡ, (ξενόω II. 3) a being abroad, Eur.

ξεροσ.def: ξερός, ή, όν (ionic for ξηρός) dry, ποτὶ ξερόν to the dry land, Od., Anth.

ξεστησ.def: ξέστης, ου, ὁ, = Lat. sextarius, nearly a pint, NTest.

ξεστοσ.def: ξεστός, ή, όν smoothed, polished, wrought, Hom., Hdt., attic; ξ. αἴθουσαι halls of polished stone, Il. (from ξέω)

ξεω.def: ξέω to smooth or polish by scraping, planing, filing, of a carpenter, Od., etc.

ξηρα.def: ξηρά (sc. γῆ) dry land, v. ξηρός III.

ξηραινω.def: ξηραίνω (ξηρός) 1. to parch up, dry up, Eur., Xen.:—Pass. to become or be dry, parched, Il., etc. 2. to lay dry, Lat. siccare, Thuc.

ξηραλοιφεω.def: ξηρ-ᾰλοιφέω, (ἀλείφω) properly to rub dry with oil, without the use of the bath, Lex ap. Plut., Aeschin.

ξηραμπελινοσ.gloss: of the colour of withered vine-leaves, bright red
ξηραμπελινοσ.def: ξηρ-αμπέλῐνος, η, ον of the colour of withered vine-leaves, bright red, Juven.

ξηροσ.def: ξηρός, ή, όν I. dry, Lat. siccus, opp. to ὑγρός, Hdt., Ar.; ξηροῖς ὄμμασι, Hor.'s siccis oculis, Aesch. 2. of bodily condition, withered, lean, haggard, δέμας Eur., Theocr. II. like Lat. siccus, fasting, austere, harsh, Eur., Ar.; ἐν ξηροῖσιν ἐκτρέφειν Eur. III. as Subst., ἡ ξηρά (sc. γῆ), dry land, Xen.; so, τὸ ξηρόν Hdt.; ναῦς ἐπὶ τοῦ ξηροῦ ποιεῖν to leave the ships aground, Thuc.

ξηροτησ.def: ξηρότης, ητος, ἡ, (ξηρός) dryness, Plat., Xen.: ἡ ξ. τῶν νεῶν the dryness, i. e. soundness, of their timbers, Thuc.

ξηροφαγεω.def: ξηρο-φᾰγέω, (φαγεῖν) to eat dry food, Anth., etc.

ξι.def: ξῖ Ξ, ξ, ξῖ, τό, indecl., fourteenth letter of the Gk. alphabet: as numeral ξʹ = 60, but ͵ξ = 60,000: introduced in the archonship of Euclides, 403 B. C.—It is a double consonant, compounded of γς, κς, or χς. Changes 1. ξ in aeolic and attic appears as an aspirated form of κ, cf. ξυνός with κοινός, ξύν with cum;— or of ς, cf. ξύν with σύν, ξέστης with Lat. sextarius; and so in doric fut. of Verbs in -ζω, κομίξω κλᾳξῶ παιξῶ for κομίσω κλῄσω παίσω. 2. interchanged with σς, ionic διξός, τριξός for δισσός, τρισσός.

ξιφηρησ.def: ξῐφ-ήρης, ες (⁎ἄρω) sword in hand, Eur.

ξιφηφοροσ.def: ξῐφη-φόρος, ον, (φέρω) sword in hand, Aesch., Eur.

ξιφιδιον.def: ξῐφίδιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of ξίφος) a dagger, Thuc., etc.

ξιφιστηρ.def: ξῐφιστηφαιλινγ ον λεμβυφ [] (ξίφος) a sword-belt, Plut.

ξιφοδηλητοσ.def: ξῐφο-δήλητος, ον, (δηλέομαι) slain by the sword, ξ. θάνατος death by the sword, Aesch.

ξιφοκτονοσ.def: ξῐφο-κτόνος, ον, (κτείνω) slaying with the sword, Soph.

ξιφοσ.def: ξῐ́φος, αεολιξ σκίφος, εος, a sword, Hom.; distinguished from μάχαιρα, q. v.

ξιφουλκια.def: ξῐφουλκία, ἡ, the drawing of a sword, Plut. (from ξῐφουλκός)

ξιφουλκοσ.def: ξῐφ-ουλκός, όν (ἕλκω) drawing a sword, Aesch.

ξοανον.def: ξόᾰνον, ου, τό, (ξέω) an image carved of wood, Xen.: generally, an image, statue, Eur.

ξοανουργια.def: ξοᾰν-ουργία, ἡ, (Ἔργω) a carving of images, Luc.

ξοισ.def: ξο̈ίς, ίδος, ἡ, (ξέω) a sculptor's chisel, anth.

ξουθοπτεροσ.def: ξουθό-πτερος, ον, (πτερόν) with tawny wings, Eur.

ξουθοσ.def: ξουθός, ή, όν I. of a colour, between ξανθός and πυρρός, yellowish, brown-yellow, tawny, epith. of the bee, Eur.; of the nightingale, Aesch., Eur., etc. II. later of sound, shrill, thrilling, Babr., Anth.

ξυηλη.gloss: a tool for scraping wood, a plane
ξυηλη.def: ξυήλη, ἡ, (ξύω) I. a tool for scraping wood, a plane or rasp, Xen. II. a sickle-shaped dagger, id.

ξυληγεω.def: ξῠληγέω, (ἄγω) to carry wood, Dem. (from ξῠληγός)

ξυληφιον.gloss: a piece of wood, a stick
ξυληφιον.def: ξῠλήφιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of ξύλον) a piece of wood, a stick, Polyb.

ξυλιζομαι.def: ξῠλίζομαι, (ξύλον) Mid. to gather wood, Xen.

ξυλινοσ.def: ξῠ́λῐνος, η, ον (ξύλον) 1. of wood, wooden, Hdt., attic 2. metaph. wooden, νοῦς Anth.

ξυλοκοπεω.gloss: to beat with a stick, cudgel
ξυλοκοπεω.def: ξῠλοκοπέω, to beat with a stick, cudgel, Polyb.

ξυλοκοπια.def: ξῠλοκοπία, ἡ, a cudgelling, Lat. fustuarium, Polyb.

ξυλοκοποσ.def: ξῠλοκόπος, ον, (κόπτω) hewing or felling wood, Xen.

ξυλον.def: ξῠ́λον, ου, τό, (perh. from ξύω) I. wood cut and ready for use, firewood, timber, Hom.; ξύλα νήια ship- timber, Hes.; ξ. ναυπηγήσιμα Thuc. II. in sg. a piece of wood, a post, Hom.: a perch, Ar.: a stick, cudgel, club, Hdt., Ar. 2. a collar of wood, put on the neck of the prisoner, Ar.:—also stocks, for the feet, Hdt., Ar.; cf. πεντεσύριγγος. 3. a plank or beam to which malefactors were bound, the Cross, NTest. 4. a money-changer's table, Dem. 5. πρῶτον ξύλον the front bench of the Athenian theatre, Ar. of live wood, a tree, Xen.

ξυλοπαγησ.def: ξῠλο-πᾰγής, ές (πήγνυμι) built of wood, Strab.

ξυλουργια.def: ξῠλουργία, ἡ, (from ξῠλουργέω) a working of wood, carpentry, Aesch.

ξυλοφορεω.def: ξῠλοφορέω, to carry a stick, as the Cynics did, Luc.

ξυλοχοσ.def: ξῠ́λ-οχος, ἡ, (perh. from ξύλον, ἔχω) a thicket, copse, Il.

ξυλωσισ.gloss: the woodwork of a house, frame-work
ξυλωσισ.def: ξύλωσις (from ξῠλόω) the woodwork of a house, frame-work, Thuc.

ξυνεεικοσι.def: ξυνεείκοσι epic for συν-είκοσι, twenty together, Od.

ξυνηιοσ.def: ξῡνήιος, η, ον (epic and ionic for ξύνειος, which does not occur) ξυνήια common property, common stock, Il.

ξυνηων.def: ξῡνήων, ονος, ὁ, (ξυνός) a joint-owner, partner in a thing, c. gen., Hes.; ξυνάονες ἑλκέων, I. e. afflicted by sores, Pind.:—absol., ξυνάν a friend, id.

ξυνοδοτηρ.def: ξῡνο-δοτηφαιλινγ ον λεμβυφ [] the free, bounteous giver, Anth.

ξυνοσ.def: ξῡνός, ή, όν (ξύν) older form of κοινός, common, public, general, concerning or belonging to all in common, Il.; γαῖα ξυνὴ πάντων earth the common property of all, id.; ξ. Ἐνυάλιος, i. e. war hath an even hand, is uncertain, id.; ξ. πᾶσι ἀγαθόν Hdt.; ξυνὰ λέγειν to speak for the common good, Aesch.

ξυνοφρων.def: ξῡνό-φρων, ονος, ὁ, ἡ, (φρήν) friendly-minded, Anth.

ξυνοχαρησ.def: ξῡνο-χᾰρής, ές (χαίρω) rejoicing in common, Anth.

ξυρεω.def: ξυρέω (ξυρόν) to shave, Hdt.: proverb. of great danger or sharp pain, ξυρεῖ ἐν χρῶι it shaves close, touches the quick, Soph.:—Mid. and Pass. to shave oneself or have oneself shaved, Hdt.; ξυρεῦνται πᾶν τὸ σῶμα they have their whole body shaved, id.

ξυρηκησ.def: ξῠρ-ήκης, ες (ἀκη) I. keen as a rasor, Xen. II. pass. close-shaven, Eur.; κουρᾷ ξυρήκει with close tonsure, id.

ξυρον.def: ξῠρόν, οῦ, (ξύω) a rasor, Hom., etc.:—proverb, ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἵσταται ἀκμῆς ὄλεθρος ἠὲ βιῶναι death or life is balanced on a rasor's edge, Il.; ἐπὶ ξυροῦ τῆς ἀκμῆς ἔχεται ἡμῖν τὰ πράγματα Hdt.; βεβὼς ἐπὶ ξυρῷ τύχης Soph.

ξυσμη.def: ξυσμή, ἡ, (ξύω) in pl., scrapings, Anth.

ξυστηρ.def: ξυστηφαιλινγ ον λεμβυφ [] (ξύω) a graving tool, Lat. scalprum, Anth.

ξυστισ.gloss: a xystis, a robe of fine material, a robe of state
ξυστισ.def: ξυστίς, αττιξ ξύστις, ίδος, ἡ, (ξύω) a xystis, a robe of fine material, a robe of state, Ar., Plat., etc.

ξυστον.def: ξυστόν, οῦ, (ξύω) 1. the polished shaft of a spear, Il., Hdt. 2. generally, a spear, lance, Il., Eur.

ξυστοσ.def: ξυστός, οῦ, ὁ, (ξύω) a covered colonnade on the S. side of the gymnasium, where athletes exercised in winter, Xen., etc.: so called from its smooth and polished floor.

ξυστοφοροσ.def: ξυστο-φόρος, ον, (φέρω) carrying a spear, Xen.

ξυω.def: ξύω (akin to ξέω) I. to scrape, plane, smooth or polish, Od.: metaph., ξῦσαι ἀπὸ γῆρας to scrape off, get rid of old age, Hhymn.:— Mid., παλτὸν ξύσασθαι to shape oneself a javelin-shaft, Xen. II. to make smooth, work delicately, Il.
